"I’ll come back to help."
"Thank you. I won't forget who fed me when it mattered."

"You said something odd the other day. Let's talk about it."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I need to ask you something."
"Okay." Amina looks down. "Okay, you got me. I wasn't an EMT. I was a Midwife. Everyone out here is selling something. I was selling a better version of me." Their voice is small.

"The whole fire was arguing about Gavel last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"I need a moment to think about that."
"Take your time."
"Go on."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"I’m listening."
"We'll land on something. We always do — usually the loudest person's idea."
"Tell me more."
"My vote? I'm keeping it to myself until the shouting stops."
"Want to come with us?"
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"Tell me why you need this."

"I’ll come back to help."
"Good — The south slope below the meadow, morning, early. Bring a pack."

"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can I ask you something else?"
